arxiv-2011-11036.title: Interpreting Super-Resolution Networks with Local Attribution Maps
arxiv-2011-11036.creator: Jinjin Gu, Chao Dong
arxiv-2011-11036.description: Abstract Image super-resolution (SR) techniques have been developing rapidly, benefiting from the invention of deep networks and its successive breakthroughs. However, it is acknowledged that deep learning and deep neural networks are difficult to interpret. SR networks inherit this mysterious nature and little works make attempt to understand them.

arxiv-2012-02138.title: Fluctuations of anisotropic flow from the finite number of rescatterings in a two-dimensional massless transport model
arxiv-2012-02138.creator: Hendrik Roch, Nicolas Borghini
arxiv-2012-02138.description: Abstract We investigate the fluctuations of anisotropic transverse flow due to the finite number of scatterings in a two-dimensional system of massless particles. Using a set of initial geometries from a Monte Carlo Glauber model, we study how flow coefficients fluctuate about their mean value at the corresponding eccentricity, for several values of the scattering cross section.

arxiv-2105-11074.title: Liouville Action for Harmonic Diffeomorphisms This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Mathematics of Integrable Systems: Classical and Quantum in honor of Leon Takhtajan. The full collection is available at https://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/Takhtajan.html
arxiv-2105-11074.creator: Jinsung PARK
arxiv-2105-11074.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce a Liouville action for a harmonic diffeomorphism from a compact Riemann surface to a compact hyperbolic Riemann surface of genus g ≥ 2 g\geq 2 . We derive the variational formula of this Liouville action for harmonic diffeomorphisms when the source Riemann surfaces vary with a fixed target Riemann surface.

arxiv-2202-10965.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Andreas Fring, Takanobu Taira, Rebecca Tenney. 𝒞 {\cal C} -operators were introduced as involution operators in non-Hermitian theories that commute with the time-independent Hamiltonians and the parity/time-reversal operator. Here we propose a definition for time-dependent 𝒞 ⁡ ( t ) {\cal C}(t) -operators and demonstrate that for a particular signature they may be expanded in terms of time-dependent biorthonormal left and right eigenvectors of Lewis-Riesenfeld invariants.

arxiv-2402-00971.creator: Aytekin Erdogan, Erdem Akagündüz
arxiv-2402-00971.description: Abstract Due to the lack of a definitive ground truth for the image fusion problem, the loss functions are structured based on evaluation metrics, such as the structural similarity index measure (SSIM). However, in doing so, a bias is introduced toward the SSIM and, consequently, the input visual band image.

arxiv-2405-12694.title: Parameter estimation methods in Comparative Judgement
arxiv-2405-12694.creator: Ian Hamilton, Nick Tawn
arxiv-2405-12694.description: Abstract Abstract Comparative Judgement is an assessment method where item ratings are estimated based on rankings of subsets of the items. These rankings are typically pairwise, with ratings taken to be the estimated parameters from fitting a Bradley-Terry model. Likelihood penalization is often employed. Adaptive scheduling of the comparisons can increase the efficiency of the assessment.

arxiv-2410-14975.creator: Jihyo Kim, Seulbi Lee *, Sangheum Hwang
arxiv-2410-14975.description: Abstract With the recent emergence of foundation models trained on internet-scale data and demonstrating remarkable generalization capabilities, such foundation models have become more widely adopted, leading to an expanding range of application domains. Despite this rapid proliferation, the trustworthiness of foundation models remains underexplored.

arxiv-2503-10439.title: EFC++: Elastic Feature Consolidation with Prototype Re-balancing for Cold Start Exemplar-free Incremental Learning
arxiv-2503-10439.creator: Simone Magistri, Tomaso Trinci, Albin Soutif–Cormerais, Joost van de Weijer, Andrew D. Bagdanov
arxiv-2503-10439.description: Abstract Exemplar-Free Class Incremental Learning (EFCIL) aims to learn from a sequence of tasks without having access to previous task data. In this paper, we consider the challenging Cold Start scenario in which insufficient data is available in the first task to learn a high-quality backbone.

arxiv-2505-13436.title: KinTwin: Imitation Learning with Torque and Muscle Driven Biomechanical Models Enables Precise Replication of Able-Bodied and Impaired Movement from Markerless Motion Capture
arxiv-2505-13436.creator: R. James Cotton
arxiv-2505-13436.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by R. James Cotton. Broader access to high-quality movement analysis could greatly benefit movement science and rehabilitation, such as allowing more detailed characterization of movement impairments and responses to interventions, or even enabling early detection of new neurological conditions or fall risk. While emerging technologies are making it easier to capture kinematics with biomechanical models, or how joint angles change over time, inferring the underlying physics that give rise to these movements, including ground reaction forces, joint torques, or even muscle activations, is still challenging.

arxiv-2505-14240.title: Learning with Local Search MCMC Layers
arxiv-2505-14240.creator: Germain Vivier-Ardisson gvivier@google.com, Mathieu Blondel mblondel@google.com, Axel Parmentier axel.parmentier@enpc.fr
arxiv-2505-14240.description: Abstract Integrating combinatorial optimization layers into neural networks has recently attracted significant research interest. However, many existing approaches lack theoretical guarantees or fail to perform adequately when relying on inexact solvers. This is a critical limitation, as many operations research problems are NP-hard, often necessitating the use of neighborhood-based local search heuristics.

pmc-11356642.title: The Stiffness and Damping Characteristics of a Rubber-Based SMA Composite Shock Absorber with a Hyper-Elastic SMA-Constitutive Model Considering the Loading Rate
pmc-11356642.creator: Yizhe Huang, Huizhen Zhang, Qiyuan Fan, Qibai Huang, Lefei Shao, Xin Zhan, Jun Wang
pmc-11356642.description: Shock absorbers are essential in enhancing vehicle ride comfort by mitigating vibrations. However, traditional rubber shock absorbers are constrained by their fixed stiffness and damping properties, limiting their adaptability to varying loads and thus affecting the ride comfort, especially under extreme road conditions.

pmc-11511735.title: Hormonal influence on maize inflorescence development and reproduction
pmc-11511735.creator: Amina Chaudhry, Zongliang Chen, Andrea Gallavotti
pmc-11511735.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Key messageDifferent plant hormones contribute to maize reproductive success.AbstractMaize is a major crop species and significantly contributes directly and indirectly to human calorie uptake. Its success can be mainly attributed to its unisexual inflorescences, the tassel and the ear, whose formation is regulated by complex genetic and hormonal networks, and is influenced by environmental cues such as temperature, and nutrient and water availability.

pmc-11643030.title: Bis-Iridoids: Occurrence, Chemophenetic Evaluation and Biological Activities—A Review
pmc-11643030.creator: Claudio Frezza, Alessandro Venditti, Daniela De Vita, Marcella Guiso, Armandodoriano Bianco, David Barker, Arjun H Banskota
pmc-11643030.description: In this work, the first review paper about bis-iridoids was presented. In particular, their detailed occurrence, chemophenetic evaluation and biological activities were reported. To the best of our knowledge, two hundred and eighty-eight bis-iridoids have been evidenced so far, bearing different structural features, with the link between two seco-iridoids sub-units as the major one.

pmc-12616923.title: Cellular osmoregulation enhances porcine embryo development by restoring zygotic genome activation via metabolic–epigenetic crosstalk
pmc-12616923.creator: Xiangyuan Zhao, Lixiang Liu, Xiaoyu Chu, Ying Zhang, Yu Tang, Jing Shao, Bingfeng Fan, Yifeng Yang, Baozeng Xu
pmc-12616923.description: IntroductionIn vitro embryo culture is essential for human assisted reproduction and livestock breeding, yet its efficiency remains limited owing to developmental arrest triggered by suboptimal media composition and environmental stressors. Preimplantation embryos are highly sensitive to a minor increase in osmolarity under organic osmolyte deficiency, which disrupts cell volume homeostasis to cause developmental block.

pmc-13212715.title: Fascicle lengthening during a large torque reduction subsequently decreases dorsiflexion torque steadiness
pmc-13212715.creator: Brent James Raiteri, Ricardo De Lorenzo, Malte Kraul, Daniel Hahn
pmc-13212715.description: Here we assessed the effect of different rates and amplitudes of active torque reduction on the subsequent steady-state EMG amplitude, torque steadiness, and fascicle length during submaximal voluntary fixed-end (isometric) dorsiflexion contractions. Based on previous findings following active muscle-tendon unit lengthening, we expected a reduced steady-state EMG amplitude and torque steadiness relative to torque-matched reference contractions.

pmc-13442378.title: An explainable machine learning model for type B aortic dissection identification: development and internal evaluation
pmc-13442378.creator: Donglin Li, Dilinuerkezi Abulimiti, Zaiying Yeerbao, Xiangxiang Ru, Xinxi Li, Lei Zhang, Jingdong Tang, Shuai Jiang, Ye Tian
pmc-13442378.description: PurposeType B aortic dissection (TBAD) is a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency that requires timely recognition. This study aimed to develop and internally evaluate an explainable machine learning model for identifying existing TBAD using routinely available clinical history and admission laboratory data.

pmc-13572969.title: Synaptic Mitochondrial Oxidative Stress Contributes to Individual Variability in Age‐Related Cognitive Inflexibility in Mice
pmc-13572969.creator: Rui Yamada, Hirotaka Nagai, Chisato Numa, Yunhui Zhu, Midori Nagai, Kohei Ota, Yusuke Kawashima, Nobuhiko Ohno, Tomoyuki Furuyashiki
pmc-13572969.description: Aging is associated with impairments in cognitive flexibility, a key executive function supported by the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), yet the biological mechanisms underlying individual variability in age‐related decline remain poorly understood. Here we investigated behavioral, ultrastructural, and proteomic correlates of cognitive inflexibility in mice across aging.

pmc-13668897.title: Temporal trends in the clinical presentation, management, and outcomes of children with congenital cytomegalovirus infection
pmc-13668897.creator: Jitka Bolchová, Despoina Gkentzi, Roberto Pedrero Tomé, Garyfallia Syridou, Antoni Noguera-Julián, María Ríos-Barnés, Serena Salomé, Francesco Raimondi, Serena Villaverde, Fernando Baquero-Artigao, Paula Rodriguez-Molino, Danilo Buonsenso, Laura Martino, Beatriz Álvarez-Vallejo, Jesús Saavedra, Yves
pmc-13668897.description: Congenital cytomegalovirus (cCMV) is the most common congenital infection and a leading cause of sensorineural hearing loss as well as neurodevelopmental impairment. In recent years, awareness, screening, and management strategies for cCMV have evolved. This study aimed to assess temporal changes in the clinical presentation, treatment, and outcomes of children diagnosed with cCMV infection.
